article.statement: A biproduct is both a product through $p_j$ and a coproduct through $i_j$. Conversely, any finite product in a preadditive category has canonical biproduct injections; any finite coproduct has canonical biproduct projections.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 3.5 [env-3-5], p. 8. The finite block maps in target §1.2 and the proof of Proposition 3.9 use the product and coproduct properties of the same object.

portal.statement:
In a preadditive category, every finite product is a biproduct. Hence for a
preadditive category the existence of all finite products, all finite
coproducts, and all finite biproducts are equivalent conditions.

article.statement:
For finite biproducts $X=\bigoplus_jX_j$, $Y=\bigoplus_kY_k$, every $f:X\to Y$ is determined by entries $f_{kj}=p^Y_k f i^X_j$, and

$$
f=\sum_{k,j}i^Y_k f_{kj}p^X_j.
$$

For $g:Y\to Z=\bigoplus_\ell Z_\ell$, composition has entries $(gf)_{\ell j}=\sum_k g_{\ell k}f_{kj}$. Addition is entrywise.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 3.7 [env-3-7], p. 9. Target §1.2 uses the entry formula to recover each evaluated block and identify stacking with block-matrix multiplication.

portal.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an additive category. Let
$f:\bigoplus_{i=1}^mA_i\to\bigoplus_{j=1}^nB_j$ have matrix
$F=(f_{ji})_{j,i}$ and let $g:\bigoplus_{j=1}^nB_j\to\bigoplus_{k=1}^rC_k$ have
matrix $G=(g_{kj})_{k,j}$. Then the matrix of $gf$ is

$$((gf)_{ki})_{k,i},\qquad (gf)_{ki}=\sum_{j=1}^ng_{kj}f_{ji}.$$

The finiteness of the middle index set is part of the statement.

article.statement: An additive functor between additive categories preserves finite biproducts. Conversely, a functor between additive categories that preserves zero objects and finite products and coproducts is additive.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 3.9 [env-3-9], p. 9. The converse supplies additivity in Lemma 10.3, and the forward direction supplies the finite-sum correspondence in target §1.3.

article.statement: If kernels and cokernels exist, $f$ is monic exactly when its kernel is a zero object, and epic exactly when its cokernel is a zero object. Equalizers of $f,g$ are kernels of $f-g$; coequalizers are cokernels of $f-g$.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 4.2 [env-4-2], p. 10. Lemma 8.3 uses the zero-kernel and zero-cokernel criteria to turn detection by Hom into monicity and epicity. The ambient additive-category convention is in §4.1, p. 10.

items.title: Normal morphisms and cancellation in both directions

article.statement: In an abelian category every monomorphism is a kernel of its cokernel, and every epimorphism is a cokernel of its kernel. Consequently a morphism which is both monic and epic is an isomorphism.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 4.5 [env-4-5], p. 11. Lemma 8.4 presents objects using an epimorphism as the cokernel of its kernel, and Lemma 8.3 uses the monic-and-epic criterion for isomorphisms.

portal.statement:
In an abelian category, every monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel, and
dually every epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel.

article.statement: A sequence $A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ is exact if and only if $q$ is a cokernel of $f$.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 4.9 [env-4-9], p. 12. In the abelian-category setting of §4.3, this identifies the sequence and cokernel formulations of right exactness used for the presentations in Theorems 5.8, 6.7 and 9.4.

article.statement: A *submodule* $U\subseteq M$ is an additive subgroup closed under the $R$-action. The cosets $M/U$ form a module with $(m+U)+(n+U)=m+n+U$ and $r(m+U)=rm+U$. The projection $q:M\to M/U$ is surjective, and every module morphism $f:M\to N$ with $f(U)=0$ factors uniquely through $q$.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 5.4 [env-5-4], p. 15. The quotient factorization constructs the tensor product in Theorem 6.2 and the concrete cokernels used in Theorems 5.8 and 6.7. Section 1.3, p. 4, and the Chapter 5 conventions, p. 14, use ordinary choice, arbitrary unital rings with unital maps, and unital modules.

portal.statement:
Let $f:M\to P$ be a module homomorphism and let $N\le M$ satisfy
$N\subseteq\ker f$. There is a unique module homomorphism

$$\bar f:M/N\longrightarrow P$$

such that $\bar f(m+N)=f(m)$, equivalently $f=\bar f\circ\pi$.

article.statement:
For $f:M\to N$, the submodules $\ker f=\{m:f(m)=0\}$ and $\operatorname{im}f=\{f(m):m\in M\}$ give the categorical kernel $\ker f\hookrightarrow M$ and cokernel $N\twoheadrightarrow N/\operatorname{im}f$. The canonical map

$$
M/\ker f\longrightarrow\operatorname{im}f,\qquad m+\ker f\longmapsto f(m)
$$

is an isomorphism. Moreover, monomorphisms are exactly injective module maps, and epimorphisms are exactly surjective module maps.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 5.5 [env-5-5], p. 15. These concrete descriptions justify the module-category abelian structure and the cokernel arguments in Lemma 8.3 and Theorem 6.7.

portal.statement:
For every module homomorphism $f:M\to N$, there is a module isomorphism

$$M/\ker f\ \cong\ \operatorname{im}f,$$

given by $m+\ker f\mapsto f(m)$.

article.statement: $R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$ is a locally small abelian category.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 5.6 [env-5-6], p. 16. Target §1.1 uses the module categories as the abelian categories on the ring side of the reconstruction and right-exact functor correspondence.

portal.statement:
For every ring $R$, the category $R\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ of left $R$-modules is
an abelian category.

article.statement: For a set-indexed family $(M_i)_{i\in I}$, the product is the set of all tuples $\prod_i M_i$, with componentwise operations. The coproduct is the *direct sum* $\bigoplus_i M_i\subseteq\prod_i M_i$, consisting of tuples with only finitely many nonzero coordinates. Their structural maps are coordinate projections and coordinate inclusions, respectively.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 5.7 [env-5-7], p. 16. The direct sum construction supplies the free copowers in Theorem 5.8, the tensor comparison in Theorem 6.6 and the Mackey sums in target §§2 and 7.4.

portal.statement:
Let $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ be left $R$-modules and $N$ a left $R$-module. For every family of homomorphisms $f_i:M_i\to N$, there is a unique homomorphism
$$f:\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i\longrightarrow N$$
such that $f\circ\jmath_i=f_i$ for every $i$. It is given by
$$f((m_i))=\sum_{i\in\operatorname{supp}(m)}f_i(m_i).$$
For $I=\varnothing$, this is the unique map $0\to N$.

article.statement:
Write $R^{(I)}=\bigoplus_{i\in I}R$, and let $e_i$ be the tuple with $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Any family $(m_i)_{i\in I}$ in $M$ determines a unique linear map $R^{(I)}\to M$ taking $e_i$ to $m_i$. Every module has an exact sequence

$$
R^{(J)}\xrightarrow{d}R^{(I)}\xrightarrow{q}M\longrightarrow0.
$$

Exactness means $\operatorname{im}d=\ker q$ and $q$ is surjective; equivalently, $q$ is a cokernel of $d$. Such a sequence is a *free presentation*.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 5.8 [env-5-8], pp. 16–17. Free modules on all elements and then on all kernel elements supply the canonical presentations in Theorems 8.6 and 9.4. The free abelian group case supplies the generators in Theorem 6.2.

portal.statement:
Let $R$ be a unital ring, $X$ a set, and $M$ a left $R$-module. Every set map $u:X\to M$ extends uniquely to an $R$-module homomorphism $\bar u:R^{(X)}\to M$ satisfying $\bar u(e_x)=u(x)$. Explicitly,
$$\bar u\left(\sum_{x\in F}r_xe_x\right)=\sum_{x\in F}r_xu(x).$$

items.title: The regular module is a small projective generator

article.statement:
Evaluation at $1$ gives a natural isomorphism of abelian groups $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,M)\cong M$. Consequently, $R$ is projective, is a generator, and is small: the canonical map

$$
\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,M_i)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R\left(R,\bigoplus_i M_i\right)
$$

is an isomorphism. Here *projective* means every map from $R$ through the target of an epimorphism lifts through that epimorphism; *generator* means $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R,-)$ distinguishes distinct morphisms; and *small* means the displayed preservation of coproducts. Also $\operatorname{End}_R(R)\cong R^{\mathrm{op}}$ as rings, with endomorphism multiplication given by composition.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 5.9 [env-5-9], p. 17. Evaluation at 1 and the opposite endomorphism ring explain the maps used in Lemmas 9.2–9.3 and the identification of the regular module in target §1.1.

portal.statement: For every unital ring $R$, evaluation at $1$ identifies endomorphisms of the left regular module with right multiplications and gives a ring isomorphism $$\operatorname{End}_R({}_R R)\cong R^{\mathrm{op}}.$$ See [[def-opposite-ring]].

article.statement:
There is an abelian group $B\otimes_R M$, with a balanced map $(b,m)\mapsto b\otimes m$, such that for every abelian group $A$, composition with this map gives a bijection

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Z}(B\otimes_R M,A)\cong\{R\text{-balanced maps }B\times M\to A\}.
$$

Every element of $B\otimes_R M$ is a finite sum of elements $b\otimes m$, called *pure tensors*. This universal property determines the tensor product up to a unique isomorphism preserving pure tensors.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 6.2 [env-6-2], p. 18. The universal property and generation by pure tensors supply the construction and equality tests for the balanced products in target §§1–2, 5–6 and 7.5. The right and left factor conventions are in Definition 6.1, p. 18.

portal.statement:
Let $R$ be a unital ring, $M$ a right $R$-module, $N$ a left $R$-module, and

$$\tau:M\times N\longrightarrow M\otimes_RN,\qquad \tau(m,n)=m\otimes n.$$

The map $\tau$ is balanced ([[def-balanced-and-bilinear-maps]]). For every abelian group $A$ and every balanced map $b:M\times N\to A$, there is a unique group homomorphism

$$\overline b:M\otimes_RN\longrightarrow A$$

such that $\overline b(m\otimes n)=b(m,n)$ for all $m,n$. Consequently composition with $\tau$ is a bijection

$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf{Ab}}(M\otimes_RN,A)\cong\operatorname{Bal}_R(M,N;A).$$

article.statement:
If $B$ is an $S$-$R$ bimodule, then $B\otimes_R M$ is a left $S$-module by $s(b\otimes m)=(sb)\otimes m$. Bimodule maps $u:B\to B'$ and left-module maps $f:M\to M'$ induce left $S$-module maps

$$
u\otimes f:B\otimes_R M\longrightarrow B'\otimes_R M',\qquad b\otimes m\longmapsto u(b)\otimes f(m).
$$

These operations form a bifunctor $(S\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}\text{-}R)\times(R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})\to S\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$, additive separately on morphisms. In particular, $B\otimes_R-$ is an additive functor.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 6.3 [env-6-3], p. 19. The induced actions and tensor maps give horizontal composition in target §1.2 and the additive functors required by Theorem 9.4.

portal.statement:
Let $M$ be a right $R$-module and let ${}_RN_S$ be an $(R,S)$-bimodule. There is a unique right $S$-module structure on $M\otimes_RN$ satisfying

$$(m\otimes n)s=m\otimes(ns).$$

Dually, if ${}_SM_R$ is an $(S,R)$-bimodule and $N$ is a left $R$-module, there is a unique left $S$-module structure satisfying

$$s(m\otimes n)=(sm)\otimes n.$$

If both outer actions are present, they commute, so the tensor product is an $(S,T)$-bimodule in the evident handed situation.

article.statement: There are natural isomorphisms $R\otimes_R M\cong M$, $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$, and $B\otimes_R R\cong B$, $b\otimes r\mapsto br$. If $B$ is an $S$-$R$ bimodule, the latter is an isomorphism of $S$-$R$ bimodules.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 6.4 [env-6-4], p. 19. The units identify empty boundaries and regular-module components in target §§1.2–1.3, and identify the regular component of the comparison in Theorem 9.4.

portal.statement:
Let $R$ be a unital ring. For every left $R$-module $N$ and every right $R$-module $M$, the maps

$$\lambda_N:R\otimes_RN\longrightarrow N,\qquad r\otimes n\longmapsto rn,$$

and

$$\rho_M:M\otimes_RR\longrightarrow M,\qquad m\otimes r\longmapsto mr,$$

are group isomorphisms. Their inverses are $n\mapsto1_R\otimes n$ and $m\mapsto m\otimes1_R$, respectively. The maps respect every displayed outer module structure.

article.statement:
Let $C$ be a $T$-$S$ bimodule, $B$ an $S$-$R$ bimodule, and $M$ a left $R$-module. Then $C\otimes_S B$ is a $T$-$R$ bimodule, and there is a natural $T$-linear isomorphism

$$
(C\otimes_S B)\otimes_R M\cong C\otimes_S(B\otimes_R M),\qquad(c\otimes b)\otimes m\longmapsto c\otimes(b\otimes m).
$$
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 6.5 [env-6-5], p. 19. Reassociation supplies the evaluated maps for rebracketing in target §1.2 and composition in target §7.5.

portal.statement:
Let $M$ be a right $R$-module, let ${}_RN_S$ be an $(R,S)$-bimodule, and let $P$ be a left $S$-module. There is a canonical group isomorphism

$$\alpha_{M,N,P}:(M\otimes_RN)\otimes_SP\longrightarrow M\otimes_R(N\otimes_SP)$$

determined by

$$\alpha_{M,N,P}((m\otimes n)\otimes p)=m\otimes(n\otimes p).$$

It respects any compatible outer module actions and is natural in $M,N,P$.

article.statement:
For every set-indexed family of left $R$-modules, the canonical $S$-linear map is an isomorphism:

$$
\bigoplus_i(B\otimes_R M_i)\longrightarrow B\otimes_R\left(\bigoplus_i M_i\right),\qquad b\otimes m_i\longmapsto b\otimes\iota_i(m_i).
$$
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 6.6 [env-6-6], p. 20. For the bimodule of Proposition 6.3, distributivity is needed in the free-module step of Theorem 9.4, in passing from the bimodule Mackey sum to the functor sum in target §2.2 and in composing sums in §7.5.

portal.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital ring and $M$ a right $A$-module. Then the functor
$T_M=M\otimes_A-:A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to\mathbf{Ab}$ is additive, preserves
cokernels (so it is right exact: every exact sequence
$X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\to0$ of left $A$-modules induces an exact
sequence $M\otimes_AX\xrightarrow{1\otimes f}M\otimes_AY\xrightarrow{1\otimes g}M\otimes_AZ\to0$),
and preserves arbitrary direct sums: the natural map
$\bigoplus_{i\in I}(M\otimes_AX_i)\to M\otimes_A(\bigoplus_{i\in I}X_i)$
induced by the coordinate inclusions is an isomorphism, including $I=\varnothing$.
If $M$ is a $(B,A)$-bimodule then $T_M$ takes values in left $B$-modules and all
the displayed maps are $B$-linear. No commutativity of $A$ or $B$ is assumed and
no choice is used.

article.statement:
If $M\xrightarrow{f}N\xrightarrow{q}Q\to0$ is exact, then

$$
B\otimes_R M\xrightarrow{1\otimes f}B\otimes_R N\xrightarrow{1\otimes q}B\otimes_R Q\longrightarrow0
$$

is exact in $S\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$. Equivalently, tensoring preserves cokernels. This property is called *right exactness*.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 6.7 [env-6-7], p. 20. For the bimodule of Proposition 6.3, right exactness puts its tensor functor in target Theorem 1.1 and carries the free-presentation comparison to all modules in Theorem 9.4.

portal.statement:
Let $A$ be a unital ring and $M$ a right $A$-module. Then the functor
$T_M=M\otimes_A-:A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to\mathbf{Ab}$ is additive, preserves
cokernels (so it is right exact: every exact sequence
$X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\to0$ of left $A$-modules induces an exact
sequence $M\otimes_AX\xrightarrow{1\otimes f}M\otimes_AY\xrightarrow{1\otimes g}M\otimes_AZ\to0$),
and preserves arbitrary direct sums: the natural map
$\bigoplus_{i\in I}(M\otimes_AX_i)\to M\otimes_A(\bigoplus_{i\in I}X_i)$
induced by the coordinate inclusions is an isomorphism, including $I=\varnothing$.
If $M$ is a $(B,A)$-bimodule then $T_M$ takes values in left $B$-modules and all
the displayed maps are $B$-linear. No commutativity of $A$ or $B$ is assumed and
no choice is used.

article.statement: This multiplication makes $k[G]$ an associative unital ring. The map $k\to k[G]$, $a\mapsto a[e]$, is an injective unital ring map whose image is central. Thus $k[G]$ is a *$k$-algebra*, meaning a ring equipped with such a central scalar map. Each $[g]$ is a unit, with inverse $[g^{-1}]$. Moreover, $k[G]$ is commutative exactly when $G$ is abelian.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 7.2 [env-7-2], p. 22. The unital ring structure, central scalars and group-basis multiplication supply the algebras and scalar actions throughout the target. The field and group conventions are on p. 21, and the multiplication is that of Definition 7.1, p. 22.

portal.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $G$ be a group. Write $[g] \in R[G]$ for
the basis vector of [[def-group-ring]] indexed by $g \in G$.

There is a unique $R$-bilinear multiplication on $R[G]$ satisfying
$$[g][h]=[gh]\qquad(g,h\in G).$$
With this product, $R[G]$ is a unital $R$-algebra whose underlying
$R$-module has basis $\{[g]:g\in G\}$. Its identity is $[e]$, where $e$ is the
identity of $G$, and every basis element $[g]$ is a unit with inverse
$[g^{-1}]$.

article.statement: There are inverse functors between $\mathrm{Rep}_k(G)$ and $k[G]\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$. The correspondence preserves the underlying abelian group and identifies intertwiners with module morphisms. It holds for arbitrary groups and arbitrary-dimensional representations.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 7.4 [env-7-4], pp. 22–23. The representation interpretation of Proposition 7.6 supplies the passage to induction and restriction of representations in target §§1.2 and 2.

portal.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $G$ be a group, and let $M$ be a left
$R$-module. Then:

1. every $R$-linear action of $G$ on $M$ extends uniquely to a left
   $R[G]$-module structure on $M$ satisfying
   $$(r[e]) \cdot m=rm\qquad(r \in R,\ m \in M);$$
2. every left $R[G]$-module structure on $M$ satisfying
   $$(r[e]) \cdot m=rm\qquad(r \in R,\ m \in M)$$
   restricts to an $R$-linear action of $G$ on $M$;
3. these two constructions are inverse to each other.

Moreover, if $M$ and $N$ carry the corresponding structures, then an
$R$-linear map $f:M \to N$ is $G$-equivariant if and only if it is an
$R[G]$-module homomorphism.

article.statement:
For a subgroup $H\subseteq G$, extending finite-support functions by zero embeds $k[H]$ into $k[G]$ as a unital subring. Thus $k[G]$ is a $k[G]$-$k[H]$ bimodule by left and right multiplication. Define

$$
\operatorname{Ind}_H^G(V)=k[G]\otimes_{k[H]}V.
$$

This is a $G$-representation by Theorem 7.4. If $W$ is a $G$-representation, let $\operatorname{Res}_H^G(W)$ denote the same vector space with its action restricted to $H$. There is a natural bijection

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{k[G]}(\operatorname{Ind}_H^G V,W)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{k[H]}(V,\operatorname{Res}_H^G W).
$$
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 7.6 [env-7-6], p. 24. The subgroup inclusion case supplies the induction bimodule and ordinary adjunction in target §§1.2 and 2.1. For conjugation embeddings the subgroup inclusion is composed with transport to its image.

portal.statement: For $H\le G$, induction is left adjoint and coinduction is right adjoint to restriction.

article.statement: If $P$ is a small projective generator, then $H$ preserves kernels and cokernels, preserves set-indexed coproducts, is faithful, and reflects isomorphisms. Here **faithful** means that its maps on Hom sets are injective, and **reflects isomorphisms** means $H(u)$ invertible implies $u$ invertible.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Lemma 8.3 [env-8-3], p. 25. Exactness and coproduct preservation carry presentations through the Hom functor in Lemma 8.5 and Theorem 8.6. Reflection of isomorphisms yields the inverse comparison in Theorem 8.6. The chapter conventions and Hom action are on p. 25.

portal.statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small cocomplete abelian category and $P$ a small projective generator of $\mathcal C$. Put $E=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(P)$, $A=E^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $H=\mathcal C(P,-):\mathcal C\to A\text{-Mod}$, where $H(Y)$ carries the left $A$-action $(e^{\mathrm{op}}\cdot h)=h\circ e$. Then:
1. $H$ is an additive functor.
2. $H$ is exact: it preserves kernels, cokernels, and every finite limit and colimit that exists in $\mathcal C$.
3. $H$ preserves every set-indexed coproduct.
4. $H$ is faithful: for all $u\neq v:X\to Y$ there is $h:P\to X$ with $uh\neq vh$.
5. If $H(Z)=0$ then $Z=0$.
No choice is used.

items.title: Every object has a generator presentation

article.statement:
For every $X$, there are sets $I,J$ and a diagram

$$
P^{(J)}\xrightarrow{d}P^{(I)}\xrightarrow{q}X\longrightarrow0
$$

in which $q$ is the cokernel of $d$. The notation $P^{(I)}$ means the coproduct of $I$ copies of $P$.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Lemma 8.4 [env-8-4], p. 26. The cokernel presentation by copies of the generator is the descent step in Lemma 8.5. The chapter hypotheses are in §8.1, p. 25.

items.title: Morphisms are determined by module maps

article.statement:
For every $X,Y$, composition induces a bijection

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(X,Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R(H(X),H(Y)),\qquad u\longmapsto H(u).
$$

Thus $H$ is **fully faithful**: its maps on Hom sets are bijections.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Lemma 8.5 [env-8-5], p. 26. The bijection lifts the maps between free modules and supplies the comparison at each object in Theorem 8.6. The chapter hypotheses are in §8.1, p. 25.

items.title: Reconstruction from a small projective generator

article.statement:
With the hypotheses and chosen constructions of §8.1,

$$
\boxed{\mathcal A\simeq R\text{-Mod},\qquad R=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal A}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}.}
$$

An **equivalence** means functors $H:\mathcal A\to R\text{-Mod}$, $L:R\text{-Mod}\to\mathcal A$, and natural isomorphisms $HL\cong1_{R\text{-Mod}}$, $LH\cong1_{\mathcal A}$. The symbol $\simeq$ does not assert equality or an isomorphism of categories.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 8.6 [env-8-6], p. 27. This is the reconstruction invoked in target §1.1 for both ambient abelian categories. Section 8.1, p. 25, uses supplied coproducts and cokernels or fixes them with global choice.

portal.statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small cocomplete abelian category and let $P$ be a small projective generator of $\mathcal C$. Assume in addition that definable assignments of copowers of $P$ (including their injections) for every set, and of cokernels (including their quotient maps) for every morphism of $\mathcal C$, are supplied. Cocompleteness alone asserts their existence individually, not such simultaneous choices. Put $E=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(P)$ and $A=E^{\mathrm{op}}$, and let $H=\mathcal C(P,-):\mathcal C\to A\text{-Mod}$ and $L:A\text{-Mod}\to\mathcal C$ be the functors of [[lem-copower-presentation-construction-is-left-adjoint-to-generator-hom]], so that $L\dashv H$. Then the unit $\eta:1_{A\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}}\Rightarrow HL$ and the counit $\varepsilon:LH\Rightarrow1_{\mathcal C}$ of this adjunction are natural isomorphisms. Consequently $H$ is an equivalence of categories with quasi-inverse $L$, and $\mathcal C$ is equivalent to the module category $A\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-equivalence-and-adjoint-equivalence-of-categories]]). No commutativity of rings is assumed and no choice is used.

article.statement:
For an additive functor $F$, the left $S$-module $B=F({}_R R)$ becomes an $S$-$R$ bimodule by

$$
b r=F(\rho_r)(b),\qquad \rho_r:R\to R,\quad \rho_r(x)=xr.
$$

Here $\rho_r$ is a left $R$-module morphism, even when $R$ is noncommutative.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Lemma 9.2 [env-9-2], p. 29. This is the action formula of target Theorem 1.1 and supplies the balancing action for Lemma 9.3.

portal.statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be unital rings and let
$F:A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to B\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ be an additive functor
([[def-additive-functor]]). On the left $B$-module $M=F(A)$ define, for
$a\in A$ and $m\in M$,

$$ma:=F(r_a)(m),$$

where $r_a:A\to A$, $r_a(x)=xa$, is right multiplication, a left $A$-linear
endomorphism of $A$. Together with the given left $B$-action this makes $M$ a
$(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]): the right $A$-action satisfies the unit,
associativity and distributivity laws of [[def-left-and-right-modules]] and
commutes with the left $B$-action. No commutativity of the rings is assumed and
no choice is used.

article.statement:
For $m\in M$, let $\lambda_m:R\to M$ be the left-module map $\lambda_m(x)=xm$. There is an $S$-linear natural transformation

$$
\tau^F_M:B\otimes_R M\longrightarrow F(M),\qquad \tau^F_M(b\otimes m)=F(\lambda_m)(b).
$$
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Lemma 9.3 [env-9-3], p. 29. With the bimodule from Lemma 9.2, the comparison defines the natural map whose components Theorem 9.4 proves invertible and whose formula Theorem 9.5 uses on transformations.

portal.statement:
Let $A,B$ be unital rings, let
$F:A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to B\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ be additive, and let $M=F(A)$
carry the $(B,A)$-bimodule structure of
[[lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action]]. For
$x\in X$ let $\ell_x:A\to X$, $\ell_x(a)=ax$. Then

$$\beta_X:M\times X\to F(X),\qquad \beta_X(m,x)=F(\ell_x)(m),$$

is balanced ([[def-balanced-and-bilinear-maps]]) and $B$-linear in $m$, so it
induces a unique group homomorphism

$$\tau_X:M\otimes_AX\to F(X),\qquad \tau_X(m\otimes x)=F(\ell_x)(m),$$

and each $\tau_X$ is $B$-linear. Moreover
$\tau:M\otimes_A-\Rightarrow F$ is natural:
$F(u)\circ\tau_X=\tau_Y\circ(1_M\otimes u)$ for every left $A$-linear
$u:X\to Y$ ([[def-natural-transformation]]). The construction of $\tau$ chooses
no presentation of $X$ and no elements.

article.statement: Every additive, right-exact, coproduct-preserving functor $F:R\text{-Mod}\to S\text{-Mod}$ is naturally isomorphic to $F(R)\otimes_R-$, through $\tau^F$. Every $S$-$R$ bimodule gives such a functor.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 9.4 [env-9-4], p. 30. The object correspondence in target Theorem 1.1 uses the regular, free and cokernel steps of this proof. The permitted functors are specified in Definition 9.1, p. 28.

portal.statement:
Let $A,B$ be unital rings.

(i) For every $(B,A)$-bimodule $M$ ([[def-bimodule]]) the functor
$T_M=M\otimes_A-:A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to B\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ is additive,
right exact, coproduct-preserving and therefore cocontinuous
([[def-additive-cocontinuous-module-functor]]), and the assignment
$M\mapsto T_M$ is functorial: a bimodule map $f:M\to M'$ gives the natural
transformation with components $f\otimes1_X$.

(ii) Conversely every additive cocontinuous functor
$F:A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to B\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ is naturally isomorphic to
$T_{F(A)}$, where $F(A)$ carries the $(B,A)$-bimodule structure
$ma=F(r_a)(m)$ ([[lem-evaluation-on-the-regular-module-has-a-commuting-right-action]]).

Hence, up to natural isomorphism, the additive cocontinuous functors are exactly
the tensor functors with bimodule kernels: the quasi-inverse of $M\mapsto T_M$
is $F\mapsto F({}_AA)$, with categorical language interpreted schematically
as in [[def-additive-cocontinuous-module-functor]]. No commutativity of $A$ or $B$ is assumed and no choice
is used.

items.title: Evaluation at R classifies every transformation

article.statement:
For permitted functors $F,G$, the assignment $\eta\mapsto\eta_R$ is a bijection

$$
\operatorname{Nat}(F,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}R}(F(R),G(R)).
$$

In particular, for bimodules $B,D$, every transformation $T_B\Rightarrow T_D$ is uniquely $\beta\otimes1$ for an $S$-$R$ bimodule morphism $\beta:B\to D$.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 9.5 [env-9-5], p. 30. Target §§1.1 and 1.3 recover transformations and diagrammatic membership from the component at the regular module. The permitted-functor and size conventions are in Definition 9.1, p. 28.

portal.statement:
Let $A,B$ be unital rings and let $M,M'$ be $(B,A)$-bimodules
([[def-bimodule]]), with tensor functors $T_M=M\otimes_A-$ and
$T_{M'}=M'\otimes_A-$. Under the tensor-unit isomorphisms
$\rho_M:M\otimes_AA\to M$ and $\rho_{M'}:M'\otimes_AA\to M'$ of
[[thm-unit-isomorphisms-for-module-tensor-products]], every natural
transformation $\eta:T_M\Rightarrow T_{M'}$ corresponds to the $B$-linear map

$$f=\rho_{M'}\circ\eta_A\circ\rho_M^{-1}:M\longrightarrow M',\qquad f(m)=\rho_{M'}\bigl(\eta_A(m\otimes1)\bigr),$$

which satisfies $f(ma)=f(m)a$ for all $a\in A$, i.e. is a $(B,A)$-bimodule
map, and then $\eta_X=f\otimes1_X$ for every left $A$-module $X$. Conversely
every bimodule map $f:M\to M'$ yields a natural transformation with components
$f\otimes1_X$. The two assignments are inverse bijections
$\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')$,
compatible with addition, identities, and vertical composition. No commutativity
and no choice are used. Here $\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})$ uses
bimodule maps as set codes for the component families, not those
proper-class families as elements of a set.

article.statement:
The assignment

$$
\mathscr B(S,R)\longrightarrow\mathscr F(R,S),\qquad B\longmapsto T_B,\qquad \beta\longmapsto\beta\otimes1,
$$

is fully faithful and essentially surjective. It has the explicit inverse assignment $F\mapsto F(R)$, $\eta\mapsto\eta_R$, with comparisons $T_{F(R)}\cong F$ and $T_B(R)\cong B$. Thus it is an equivalence in the componentwise size convention of Definition 9.1.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Corollary 9.6 [env-9-6], p. 31. This assembles the equivalence and its inverse in target Theorem 1.1, and is the module-category equivalence transported by Theorem 10.4. Definition 9.1, p. 28, supplies the componentwise size convention.

portal.statement:
Let $A,B$ be unital rings. The assignment $M\mapsto T_M$ extends to an
schematic equivalence between the category of $(B,A)$-bimodules with
bimodule maps ([[def-bimodule]]) and the category of additive cocontinuous
functors $A\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}\to B\text{-}\mathbf{Mod}$ with natural
transformations
([[lem-additive-cocontinuous-module-functors-form-a-category]]). It is full and
faithful with
$\operatorname{Nat}(T_M,T_{M'})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{B\text{-}A}(M,M')$,
naturally in $M$ and $M'$, and essentially surjective by
[[thm-eilenberg-watts-for-arbitrary-unital-rings]]; a quasi-inverse is
$F\mapsto F({}_AA)$. In particular $T_M\cong T_{M'}$ if and only if
$M\cong M'$ as $(B,A)$-bimodules. Categorical language has the schematic meaning of
[[def-additive-cocontinuous-module-functor]]; no category with proper-class
functors as set-coded objects is asserted. No commutativity and no choice are used.

article.statement:
Let ${}_S B_R$ and ${}_T C_S$ be bimodules. Their tensor product $C\otimes_S B$ is a $T$-$R$ bimodule, with

$$
t(c\otimes b)=(tc)\otimes b,\qquad(c\otimes b)r=c\otimes(br).
$$

There are natural isomorphisms

$$
T_C\circ T_B\cong T_{C\otimes_S B},\qquad T_{{}_R R_R}\cong1_{R\text{-Mod}}.
$$

They send $c\otimes(b\otimes m)$ to $(c\otimes b)\otimes m$, and $r\otimes m$ to $rm$, respectively.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 10.1 [env-10-1], p. 32. This gives the composition and regular-identity clauses of target Theorem 1.1 and the reassociation used in target §7.5.

portal.statement:
Write $\mathbf{RngMod}$ for the schematic strict 2-category with object labels the unital rings $A$, interpreted as the module categories $A\text{-Mod}$, whose 1-cells are the additive cocontinuous functors $A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-additive-cocontinuous-module-functor]]), and whose 2-cells are all natural transformations, with vertical and horizontal composition as in [[def-horizontal-composition-and-whiskering-of-natural-transformations]], so that $\mathbf{RngMod}(A\text{-Mod},B\text{-Mod})$ is the functor category $\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathrm{coc}}_{\mathrm{add}}(A\text{-Mod},B\text{-Mod})$ of [[lem-additive-cocontinuous-module-functors-form-a-category]]. Here the category and strict 2-category laws are interpreted componentwise for fixed definable functor schemas, as in [[def-additive-cocontinuous-module-functor]]: no category whose objects are proper-class functors is formed. The pseudofunctor terminology asserts the equations of [[def-bicategory-pseudofunctor-and-biequivalence]] in this schematic sense. Then the assignment
$$\Phi(A)=A\text{-Mod},\qquad \Phi(M)=T_M=M\otimes_A-,\qquad \Phi(f)=f\otimes1,$$
for a unital ring $A$, a $(B,A)$-bimodule $M$, and a bimodule map $f$, is a pseudofunctor $\Phi:\mathbf{Bimod}\to\mathbf{RngMod}$ ([[def-bicategory-pseudofunctor-and-biequivalence]]): its composition comparison is the associativity isomorphism $T_N\circ T_M\cong T_{N\otimes_BM}$ with components $N\otimes_B(M\otimes_AX)\cong(N\otimes_BM)\otimes_AX$, its identity comparison is $X\to A\otimes_AX$, $x\mapsto1_A\otimes x$, and the pseudofunctor coherence equations hold. Moreover horizontal composition of 2-cells corresponds to tensoring bimodule maps, $\phi_{N\prime,M\prime}\,(\Phi(g)*\Phi(f))=\Phi(g\otimes f)\,\phi_{N,M}$, so vertical and horizontal composition satisfy the interchange law ([[thm-interchange-law-for-natural-transformations]]). No commutativity and no choice are used.

article.statement: These comparisons are coherent: for four tensor factors, each route through repeated reassociation sends any pure tensor to the same rebracketing with the same four entries. Pure tensors generate every iterated tensor product, so the routes agree as maps. This verifies the associativity pentagon directly. Removing a middle regular-ring factor either by its action first or by reassociation first gives the same tensor by balancing; this verifies the unit triangle.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 10.1, unnumbered coherence assertion in its proof [env-10-1], p. 32. The associativity pentagon and unit triangle supply bicategory coherence for target Corollary 7.5.

portal.statement:
The data of [[def-morita-bicategory-of-rings-and-bimodules]] satisfy the bicategory axioms of [[def-bicategory-pseudofunctor-and-biequivalence]]. Explicitly: for a $(D,C)$-bimodule $H$, a $(C,B)$-bimodule $G$, and a $(B,A)$-bimodule $F$ the canonical associativity isomorphisms are natural isomorphisms of bimodules
$$\alpha_{H,G,F}:(H\otimes_CG)\otimes_BF\longrightarrow H\otimes_C(G\otimes_BF);$$
the unitors $B\otimes_BF\cong F$ and $F\otimes_AA\cong F$ are natural isomorphisms; the pentagon and triangle identities hold; and horizontal composition of bimodule maps, $(g,f)\mapsto g\otimes f$, is a functor on hom-categories that preserves identities and composition. Consequently the composition functors, associator, and unitors make the Morita data a genuine bicategory: every tensor is a finite sum of elementary tensors, on which the coherence diagrams are checked, and the two sides of each diagram agree on all elements. No commutativity of the rings and no choice are used.

article.statement:
For bimodule morphisms $\beta:B\to B'$, $\gamma:C\to C'$ with the same ring types, composition of their associated functor transformations is represented by

$$
\gamma\otimes\beta:C\otimes_SB\to C'\otimes_SB',\qquad c\otimes b\longmapsto\gamma(c)\otimes\beta(b).
$$
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Proposition 10.2 [env-10-2], p. 32. This identifies horizontal diagram composition with horizontal composition of natural transformations in target §§1.2–1.3.

portal.statement:
Write $\mathbf{RngMod}$ for the schematic strict 2-category with object labels the unital rings $A$, interpreted as the module categories $A\text{-Mod}$, whose 1-cells are the additive cocontinuous functors $A\text{-Mod}\to B\text{-Mod}$ ([[def-additive-cocontinuous-module-functor]]), and whose 2-cells are all natural transformations, with vertical and horizontal composition as in [[def-horizontal-composition-and-whiskering-of-natural-transformations]], so that $\mathbf{RngMod}(A\text{-Mod},B\text{-Mod})$ is the functor category $\mathrm{Fun}^{\mathrm{coc}}_{\mathrm{add}}(A\text{-Mod},B\text{-Mod})$ of [[lem-additive-cocontinuous-module-functors-form-a-category]]. Here the category and strict 2-category laws are interpreted componentwise for fixed definable functor schemas, as in [[def-additive-cocontinuous-module-functor]]: no category whose objects are proper-class functors is formed. The pseudofunctor terminology asserts the equations of [[def-bicategory-pseudofunctor-and-biequivalence]] in this schematic sense. Then the assignment
$$\Phi(A)=A\text{-Mod},\qquad \Phi(M)=T_M=M\otimes_A-,\qquad \Phi(f)=f\otimes1,$$
for a unital ring $A$, a $(B,A)$-bimodule $M$, and a bimodule map $f$, is a pseudofunctor $\Phi:\mathbf{Bimod}\to\mathbf{RngMod}$ ([[def-bicategory-pseudofunctor-and-biequivalence]]): its composition comparison is the associativity isomorphism $T_N\circ T_M\cong T_{N\otimes_BM}$ with components $N\otimes_B(M\otimes_AX)\cong(N\otimes_BM)\otimes_AX$, its identity comparison is $X\to A\otimes_AX$, $x\mapsto1_A\otimes x$, and the pseudofunctor coherence equations hold. Moreover horizontal composition of 2-cells corresponds to tensoring bimodule maps, $\phi_{N\prime,M\prime}\,(\Phi(g)*\Phi(f))=\Phi(g\otimes f)\,\phi_{N,M}$, so vertical and horizontal composition satisfy the interchange law ([[thm-interchange-law-for-natural-transformations]]). items.title: Equivalences preserve the hypotheses on functors

article.statement: An equivalence between abelian categories is additive and preserves kernels, cokernels, and all existing set-indexed coproducts. In particular it is exact and carries small projective generators to small projective generators.
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Lemma 10.3 [env-10-3], p. 33. Theorem 10.4 needs preservation of additivity, right exactness and coproducts under transport in both directions.

portal.statement: Every equivalence between abelian categories is exact.

article.statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal D$ be locally small abelian categories with all set-indexed coproducts and small projective generators $P,Q$. Supply the chosen constructions of Chapter 8. Put

$$
R=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal A}(P)^{\mathrm{op}},\qquad S=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal D}(Q)^{\mathrm{op}}.
$$

The category of additive, right-exact, coproduct-preserving functors $\mathcal A\to\mathcal D$, with natural transformations, is equivalent to $\mathscr B(S,R)$, in the size convention of Chapter 9. Explicitly, if $H_{\mathcal A},L_{\mathcal A}$ and $H_{\mathcal D},L_{\mathcal D}$ are the equivalences of Chapter 8, then a functor $F$ corresponds to

$$
B_F=H_{\mathcal D}\bigl(F(L_{\mathcal A}(R))\bigr),
$$

with its right $R$-action obtained by applying $H_{\mathcal D}F L_{\mathcal A}$ to $\rho_r$. A bimodule $B$ corresponds to

$$
L_{\mathcal D}\circ(B\otimes_R-)\circ H_{\mathcal A}.
$$
article.locator: Ian X, Abelian Categories and Bimodules, Theorem 10.4 [env-10-4], p. 33. This transports the module correspondence to the abstract abelian categories of target §1.1. The image of the regular module under the inverse reconstruction is the chosen generator, giving the displayed formula there. The conventions are in §8.1, p. 25, and Definition 9.1, p. 28.

Module and tensor routes. For 5.8 use Finsupp.linearCombination on the underlying module and again on the kernel of its evaluation. Membership in the range is membership in that kernel, with the converse furnished by the singleton of a kernel element. Bundle the result as a cokernel. For 5.9, import Proofs.SmallProjectiveGenerator and use SmallProjectiveGenerator_regular for (B : Type v) [Ring B] in ModuleCat.{v} B, with Projective, IsSeparator and preservation of each Discrete I coproduct by the additive-group coyoneda for I : Type v. Evaluation at one and the opposite endomorphism ring are covered by the listed Mathlib declarations. Keep the indexing universe explicit and use ULift when interpreting a regular module in a larger module-carrier universe.

For 6.2 import Proofs.ModuleTensorUniversalProperty. ModuleTensorUniversalProperty is quantified over R : Type u [Ring R], M : Type v and N : Type w with AddCommGroup, Module Rᵐᵒᵖ M and Module R N, and arbitrary target A : Type z [AddCommGroup A]. It uses the additive quotient of (M × N) →₀ ℤ by the subgroup generated by the two additivity relations and balance. It proves balance, unique additive lifts and the required equivalence with balanced maps; recover pure-tensor generation from quotient representatives and absorb integer coefficients in the first factor. The proof uses propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. For 6.3–6.5 reuse Proofs.BimoduleTensorBicategoryCoherence and Proofs.BalancedTensorAssociativity. The former packages the tensor action, pure map, balanced lift, tensor maps, associator, unitors, naturality, pure generation, pentagon and triangle on arbitrary RingCat.{u} rings and AddCommGrpCat.{u} carriers equipped with both commuting actions via Bimodule. Its FreeAddGroup/addConGen quotient has the same universal property, which gives the comparison to the 6.2 quotient. It packages data under existentials. Its axiom audit has propext and Quot.sound. BalancedTensorAssociativity handles arbitrary R and S with the first right R-module, a middle left R/right S module with commuting actions, and a last left S-module. Its association and naturality apply to supplied inner quotient actions satisfying the stated pure-generator formulas. Use the 6.3 formulas to supply those actions. For outer linearity, use the separately stated endpoint data or pure-generator extensionality. Its audit has propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. In mixed universes use the explicitly typed quotient, supplying induced outer actions on pure generators, and use the packaged same-universe coherence once the chosen model is identified by the universal property. Separate additivity of tensor maps follows by the pure-tensor formula. For 6.6 use the finite support of a single direct-sum element to define the inverse for an arbitrary index type. For 6.7 descend the balanced pair map into the quotient by the range of the tensor of f, compare with the tensor of the range quotient, and use cokernel exactness.

Reconstruction route. Use preadditiveCoyonedaObj P with coefficient ring (End P)ᵐᵒᵖ. For 8.3, its kernel comparison follows from preservation of limits. The pinned projective coyoneda finite-colimit instance supplies cokernel preservation. For the cokernel presentation map q, H(q) is epic by this preservation and is therefore surjective in modules. Smallness supplies the coproduct comparison on underlying additive groups, and the comparison already preserves the module action by postcomposition. Faithfulness is precisely separation. Detection of zero follows by comparing identity and zero, and the kernel/cokernel tests then reflect isomorphisms. For 8.4 make the evaluation cofan map indexed by all maps P ⟶ X and apply the separator condition. Repeat for the kernel and transport the cokernel along the equivalent annihilator test after an epi. For 8.5 use smallness on the free copower, the universal property of this copower and of a free module, and descend the lifted map along the generator presentation. For 8.6 use the canonical presentation on every module, lift its relation map by full faithfulness and take the chosen cokernel. The comparison from applying H identifies two cokernels. Either construct L on morphisms by transporting the free maps on generators, as in the notes, or use full faithfulness to transport morphisms through the explicit object comparisons. The comparison at objects of the source then follows by full faithfulness and reflection of isomorphisms. Keep the unit/counit data natural and preserve the identification H(P) ≅ R. Import NotesProofs.ClassicalReconstruction for the compiled root declaration ClassicalReconstruction. It factors through ReconstructionCheck.PointwiseReconstruction from NotesProofs.ReconstructionSupport. It assumes preadditivity, existence of all (v,v)-small colimits, finite products, kernels and cokernels, mono and epi normality, Projective P, IsSeparator P and preservation of v-indexed coproducts by the underlying additive Hom functor. It additionally takes chosen Type v copowers of P and cokernels with Hom equivalences and their component formulas, a functor L with a supplied adjunction unit and counit and both triangles, isomorphisms from the specified presentation cokernels to L(V), and the stated unit formula on each x. It can package those data as natural inverses after those hypotheses have been supplied. It does not supply the adjunction and must not be used as the full reconstruction theorem. Its axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

Watts and transport routes. Import Proofs.RegularModuleRightAction for RegularModuleRightAction with arbitrary rings A : Type u and B : Type v, additive F : ModuleCat.{max u z} A ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} B and regular object ULift.{z} A. It yields the right module action commuting with the unchanged left B-action, by conjugating right multiplication along ULift.moduleEquiv and applying F. It uses propext and Quot.sound. Import Proofs.CanonicalWattsComparison for CanonicalWattsComparison under the same hypotheses. It gives biadditivity, balance and outer linearity of F(λ_x)(m), a quotient tensor functor with pure action and map formulas, and a natural comparison to F composed with the codomain ULift functor in the common larger carrier universe, with uniqueness on pure generators. It uses propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and has no invertibility or preservation conclusion. For the existing comparison take a common carrier universe containing both rings and the domain carriers. In that universe identify the lifted codomain functor with F using the module equivalence between each lifted carrier and the original carrier. Identify the quotient models through their balanced universal properties. For 9.4 prove invertibility at the regular object with the unit, then at free copowers with the verified cofan helper and finally at the presentation cokernel via the naturality square and both cokernel universal properties. The project also has NotesProofs.presentation_comparison_of_cokernels in NotesProofs.PresentationCokernel as a checked module-level realization of the final chase. Its ring and six module carriers are fixed, the carriers share one universe, the two squares commute, the top composite vanishes, the bottom factorization and both cancellation hypotheses hold, the relations comparison is surjective, and the generators comparison is bijective. The result is bijectivity of the final comparison. It uses propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. These hypotheses must come from right exactness, naturality and the free cases.

For 9.5 import Proofs.NaturalTransformationsOfTensorFunctors. Its theorem assumes arbitrary rings A and B, bimodules presented with the existing left B-module structure and commuting right A-actions, and three supplied tensor functors with the pure map, the unique B-linear factorization of balanced pairings and the map formula at all modules. It gives the unit formulas and classification of natural graphs between tensor functors, including vertical composition. It uses propext and Quot.sound. For ordinary NatTrans use graph conversion or the same pure formulas and transport along the 9.4 natural isomorphisms for arbitrary permitted F and G. For 9.6 assemble the evaluation and tensor comparisons as natural in functors and bimodules. At 10.1–10.2 use the induced outer actions and compare natural isomorphisms or transformations on pure generators, using the checked coherence result for the pentagon and triangle. For 10.3 transport smallness by the explicit Hom and coproduct comparison, and use equivalence instances for the categorical preservation clauses. For 10.4 whisker the equivalences and their comparison maps and compose with 9.6. These routes provide the ingredients for checked importable connections to the target. They neither assert the historical choice-free reconstruction or Watts endpoints nor use any unproved paper conclusion.
